Definition: from G4862 and the base of G939; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place):--be(-fall), happen (unto).
BiblicalUsage: Paul speaks of the temptations which befell him by the lying in wait of the Jews as he served the Lord with humility and tears, and Peter tells suffering believers not to think it strange when the fiery trial comes, as though some strange thing had happened to them. Things befall God's people, and the befalling itself is no sign He has left them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe trials that befall me are not strange accidents but the ordinary road of following Christ, and I hold that God is in them with me.
